name: Manus Koro
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Manus Koro (bowa1234) is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's only title hit, Gibbon 2006 'Time Types and Time Trees', is a Glottolog auto-tagging false positive (Glottolog's ref page: 'computerized assignment from \"temporally\"' to Papitalai [pat]); the open author preprint (30 pp., downloaded from Gibbon's Bielefeld page and saved with text under is a rhythm/time-tree modelling paper on English and Brazilian Portuguese data with no mention of Koro/Manus/Papitalai and no word-stress placement statement for any language. Publisher copy is closed (Semantic Scholar, Crossref, OpenAlex all report no OA location; archive.org and Google Books have no full-text copy), but nothing is lost since the preprint was read. The files already held by the project from the earlier reading (Cleary-Kemp 2015 dissertation, Cleary-Kemp 2014 BLS 40, Blust 2021 front matter and Loniu sketch) were re-a full-text search for stress/accent: Cleary-Kemp's phonology sketch (syllable structure CV / CV(C), final devoicing) contains no stress statement; Blust 2021 has no Koro/Papitalai sketch (the Loniu sketch's penultimate-stress statement is about Loniu, citing Hamel 1994). No first-hand statement of word-stress placement in Manus Koro was found in this search of works with stress in the title; the language remains without a stress source. in the save directory was extended with the new files and a note on the false-positive tag.

earlier_scan.source_named: Cleary-Kemp, Jessica. 2015. Serial Verb Constructions Revisited: A Case Study from Koro. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley (includes grammar/phonology sketch).

sources.citation: Cleary-Kemp, Jessica. 2015. Serial Verb Constructions Revisited: A Case Study from Koro. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. 322 pp. (eScholarship item 3kx006xq)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.3 (pp. 16-18) gives consonant and vowel inventories (Tables 1.4-1.5), syllable structure ('CV word-internally and CV(C) word-finally'), word-final trill devoicing, neutralization of labialization word-finally, optional anticipatory vowel harmony, and a working orthography; the author notes 'A thorough phonological analysis of the language has yet to be undertaken' (fn. 6). No statement on word stress/accent anywhere in the 322 pp; the only 'stress' hits (p. 143) concern Kele and Paamese, not Koro.
